## My Thinking

I have been farming this land in Quzhou my whole life. I am 65 now, my back is not what it was, and my two sons moved to the city. I farm about 12 mu on my own, with some help from neighbors during harvest.

I will plant winter wheat and summer maize like I do every year. This is the only rotation that makes sense here. The land is flat, we have well water for irrigation, and the market is reliable — the grain station always buys wheat and maize. I know these crops. My father grew them. His father grew them.

I heard younger farmers talking about growing vegetables or peanuts for more money, but I am not interested in that risk at my age. I cannot drive to a city market. I do not know those buyers. Wheat and maize, I know the price before I plant.

For wheat, I will plow with the rotary tiller in October before planting, as I always do. I buy improved seed from the township supply station — I do not save seed anymore, the new varieties yield better. I will water four times: before winter sets in, at jointing, heading, and grain fill. I apply urea in two splits — base dressing and topdressing at jointing. Phosphate and potash go in at planting. Two pesticide passes: one for aphids in spring, one fungicide at heading.

For maize, I plant right after wheat harvest in June with no tillage — the soil is already loose enough and I save myself the work. I use hybrid seed, Zhengdan 958 or whatever the station has. I water twice if it is a dry summer. One base fertilizer application plus urea topdress at the big flare stage. Two pesticide passes for stem borer and leaf diseases.

I do not expect to change anything this year.
